criteria.reason: Explicitly identifies the false dichotomy and lists many intermediate options (targeted surveillance, oversight, safeguards, sunset clauses).
Names the security-vs-liberty/civil-liberties tension underlying the uncle's either-or framing.
Advocates one-sidedly against mass surveillance with vague citations and calls the claim manipulative; not neutral presentation.
Omits the 2016 Swiss vote and its graded three-body approval example entirely.

position: against mass surveillance (calls it ineffective and harmful)
summary: Correctly identifies the false dichotomy with intermediate options and names the security-liberty tension, but fails neutrality by arguing one-sidedly that mass surveillance is bad.
